priorFindingsResolution.note: Confirmed on disk: healthcheck-lib.sh:37 now reads `rm -rf "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null||true; mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || return 0` in the stale-lock (lage>=10) branch, replacing the old rmdir. rm -rf succeeds on a non-empty directory (unlike rmdir), so a stale lock left behind by an abnormally-killed prior run -- which is non-empty because it contains an 'owner' file per the FIND-020 fix -- can now be removed and re-created. Traced the full sequence: rm -rf removes it -> mkdir recreates it -> owner-file write + sleep 0.2 + re-read (lines 43-44, unchanged from round 5, still correctly resolves the FIND-020 concurrent-racer TOCTOU: mkdir is atomic so exactly one racer wins, and the trap at line 45 is installed only AFTER the ownership re-check passes) -> RETURN trap cleans up on exit. The FIND-013 recovery invariant (a lock older than 10min is always stealable, restoring self-heal after any single hard-kill) now holds again with no regression to the FIND-020 fix. Also confirmed $LOOP (the string interpolated into LOCK_DIR='/tmp/.$LOOP-healthcheck.lock') is a fixed literal set once per wrapper script (capafy-loop-healthcheck.sh:6 'HC_LOOP="capafy-loop"', reddit-loop-healthcheck.sh:6, life-manager-loop-healthcheck.sh:8) -- not attacker-controlled or derived from any external/network input -- so rm -rf on that path introduces no new path-injection risk.

priorFindingsResolution.note: self-fix.sh:33-45 replaced the round-5 'esc to interrupt present = continue' check with a pane-content cksum comparison across successive past-ceiling checks, intended to distinguish real progress (content changed) from a hang (content frozen). This DOES fix the narrow round-5 scenario where the pane is truly static. It does NOT fix the realistic hang scenario this round explicitly asked to verify: the Claude Code CLI's own status line embeds a continuously-incrementing elapsed-time/token counter (documented by the builder's own fixtures in test-healthcheck-lib.sh:16,29 -- '...Brewed for 3m...', '...(7m · ↓ 19k tokens · ...)') that changes every render tick regardless of whether the awaited tool call is making real progress. Because that counter text is inside the same last-25-lines block that gets cksum'd, a genuinely deadlocked fixer (e.g. a hung browser waitForSelector or network call with no timeout -- explicitly the class of work this fixer's own TASK text at self-fix.sh:51-58 assigns it) will still show a different cksum on every check purely from the ticking clock, so the code perpetually takes the 'real progress, continue' branch and never reaches the kill+respawn branch. See FIND-029 for full trace and failure scenario.

finalAssessment.decisiveQuestion: Is the system NOW sound to run unattended (self-heal + self-improve + honest verification, no human, no permanent-disable path)?
finalAssessment.summary: FIND-026 is genuinely and fully resolved this round: the stale-lock steal path now uses rm -rf, correctly handling the non-empty lock directory that the FIND-020 owner-file fix introduced, restoring the FIND-013 recovery invariant (a single hard-kill can no longer permanently and silently disable self-heal for a loop) with no new path-injection risk, since the loop-name variable is a fixed literal at every call site. This is real, positive, disk-verified progress. FIND-027, however, is NOT resolved -- it has only changed shape. The round-6 patch (comparing pane-content cksums across successive past-ceiling checks) correctly handles a fixer whose pane is truly static, but fails on the realistic hang scenario this fixer is explicitly built to encounter: a stuck browser/network call while the Claude Code CLI's own status line keeps incrementing an elapsed-time/token counter every render tick (documented by the builder's own test fixtures elsewhere in this same codebase). Because that counter sits inside the exact text block being cksum'd, the comparison will show 'changed' on virtually every check regardless of real progress, so the 180-minute kill ceiling this mechanism exists to enforce is effectively inert against the most likely real-world hang -- reproducing, in a new form, the same class of failure (a code path with no working escape hatch for a stuck subprocess) that FIND-026 was just fixed for. Compounding this, the test suite added for FIND-028 does not exercise the actual re-patched logic in either direction: the hang-detection branch has zero test coverage (the DRYRUN seam exits before reaching it), and the lock-steal test that does exist checks generic filesystem behavior and a source-string grep rather than invoking the real recovery function -- so a GREEN test run provides no real assurance about either of the two mechanisms this round was asked to verify. Given a critical, code-verifiable, disk-traceable defect (FIND-029) that directly contradicts the CLAIM's core 'no human, no babysitting, self-heal' promise for the realistic hang class this fixer will actually encounter, overall verdict is FAIL.
